title: Tensor multiplication realizes the locally generated ideal on a ringed space
statement: Let $X$ be a topological space, $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings, $\mathcal B$ a commutative $\mathcal O$-algebra sheaf [def-weil-pbc-ringed-space-algebra-module], $\mathcal E$ a sheaf of $\mathcal O$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and $e:\mathcal E\to\mathcal B$ an $\mathcal O$-linear map. Let $\mathcal T=\mathcal B\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal E$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], with canonical maps $t_U:\mathcal B(U)\otimes_{\mathcal O(U)}\mathcal E(U)\to\mathcal T(U)$. There is a unique $\mathcal O$-linear map $\mu:\mathcal T\to\mathcal B$ such that $\mu_U(t_U(b\otimes s))=b e_U(s)$ on every open $U$. The categorical module image $\mathcal I=\operatorname{Im}\mu\subseteq\mathcal B$ is an ideal subsheaf: $\mathcal I(U)$ is an ideal of $\mathcal B(U)$ for every open $U$. Explicitly, $a\in\mathcal B(U)$ belongs to $\mathcal I(U)$ if and only if each $x\in U$ has an open neighbourhood $V\subseteq U$ on which $a|_V=\sum_{j=1}^{n}b_j e_V(s_j)$ for some $n\geq0$, $b_j\in\mathcal B(V)$ and $s_j\in\mathcal E(V)$. It is the smallest ideal subsheaf containing every $e_U(\mathcal E(U))$: for every ideal subsheaf $\mathcal K\subseteq\mathcal B$ containing these images on all opens, $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal K$.

proof.text: Construct the restriction-compatible presheaf morphism P(U)=B(U) tensor E(U) → B(U) by TensorProduct.lift of (b,s) ↦ b e(s). Additivity follows from distributivity; scalar compatibility uses commutativity of B and linearity of e; naturality uses multiplicativity of restrictions and naturality of e. Apply the module-sheafification adjunction directly to obtain μ, whose pure-tensor formula follows from its unit equation. For uniqueness use injectivity of the adjunction hom equivalence and TensorProduct.ext on every open.

proof.text: The underlying additive map of the module-sheafification unit P → P# is the ordinary sheafification map. Mathlib Presheaf.imageSieve_mem says it is locally surjective. Opens.mem_grothendieckTopology therefore supplies a neighbourhood V of any x and z in P(V) mapping to the restriction of a tensor section. TensorProduct.exists_sum_tmul_eq writes z as a finite sum of pure tensors (including the empty sum). This avoids stalks and does not assert surjectivity on a fixed open.

proof.text: First prove local membership in any mono i:F→G is global membership: the categorical cokernel kills the section locally, hence globally by separatedness, and the exact sequence F→G→coker(i) remains exact under section evaluation because i is mono and evaluation preserves kernels. For any epi f the canonical map q to the sheafified sectionwise cokernel annihilates f, so q=0; the sheaf-cokernel local-image theorem then gives local lifts of every section. Apply this to the epic factorThruImage μ. Naturality of image.ι μ gives that membership in its sectionwise range is equivalent to local lifting to the tensor; the converse follows from local-to-global membership for the mono image.ι μ. Empty opens are covered by separatedness as well.

proof.text: Suppose $a\in\mathcal I(U)$ and fix $x\in U$. Step 3 lifts $a$ locally to $u\in\mathcal T(V_0)$. Apply step 2 to $u$ at $x$ and restrict to its neighbourhood $V\subseteq V_0$. Linearity and naturality of $\mu$, followed by step 1, give $a|_V=\mu_V(u|_V)=\sum_{j=1}^n b_j e_V(s_j)$. Conversely, if such a sum represents $a|_V$, put $u=\sum_{j=1}^n t_V(b_j\otimes s_j)$; then step 1 gives $\mu_V(u)=a|_V$. Doing this at each $x\in U$ supplies exactly the local lifts in step 3. This proves both directions of the asserted formula, with $n=0$ represented by $u=0$.

source.place: Tag 05JS, lemma-algebra-directed-colimit-finite-presentation, proof: ideal generated by the finite-type submodule; explicit argument from steps 1-3

proof.text: The sectionwise range of image.ι μ is already the range of a linear map, hence contains zero and is closed under addition. To prove closure under multiplication by c in B(U), use the local finite-sum criterion and replace each b_j by (c restricted to V)b_j. Multiplicativity of restriction, distribution over a finite sum, and associativity prove the required expression. These data define an Ideal of B(U) with exactly the indicated range as its carrier.

source.place: Tag 05JS, lemma-algebra-directed-colimit-finite-presentation, proof: generated ideal; ideal axioms checked using step 4

proof.text: For each s, μ(1 tensor s)=e(s). The categorical image factorization thus supplies a section of the image mapping to e(s). For a mono ideal subsheaf K containing e(E), apply the finite-sum criterion to an image section a. Every local expression sum b_j e(s_j) belongs to the ideal giving the range of K(V)→B(V), by ideal multiplication and finite-sum closure. Hence a belongs locally to that mono range; the local-to-global mono-range lemma from step 3 proves its membership on U. The argument includes the empty open.
